research_rationale: EO 8226 (August 24, 1939, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held Federal Register text, amends section 15 of EO 7845 of March 21, 1938 (annual leave regulations) to read as follows (a rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments without a break in service are entitled to stated annual leave), and the order is effective as of June 30, 1939. EO 8384 (March 29, 1940; 5 FR 1253, issue of Tuesday, April 2, 1940) prescribes new annual leave regulations and, in its section 21, states "This order shall supersede" EO 7845, EO 7879 and EO 8226 and the order is "effective as of March 2, 1940", except as to its own sections 6 and 9. EO 8226 has no term of its own, so the first end is that express supersession.
savings_reason: The substance of EO 8226 continues in the superseding order: section 15 of EO 8384 carries the same rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month and are credited with accrued leave. Leave earned under EO 8226 between June 30, 1939 and March 2, 1940 is an accrued effect; the held EO 8384 text provides for adjustment of leave on the basis of its regulations in section 21 and no held source shows any loss of leave earned under EO 8226.

The effective-as-of wording in EO 8384 section 21 reaches back before the signing date (March 29, 1940) to March 2, 1940, and the claim records March 2, 1940 as the effective date of the supersession as the order's own words state; March 29, 1940 is the alternative reading for a reviewer who treats the retroactive date as not governing.

The order was not amended or extended before its supersession. The restated section is standing text; if the amending command is read as fully performed on signing, the whole-order end date would not change because the order's only row is that restated section.

research_rationale: EO 8168 (June 14, 1939, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held Federal Register text (printed number 8168), transfers lands at Sitka, Alaska, from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of Commerce. Its operative words revoke the Executive order of August 12, 1898 and reserve the lands that order described for the Coast and Geodetic Survey as a magnetic and seismological observatory site. It states no term or condition. EO 8854 (August 16, 1941), held Federal Register text, revokes EO 8168 by number in its section 1 and, in its section 2, withdraws and reserves the same lands and an adjoining tract for the same agency and purpose. The first end of EO 8168 is that express revocation. Prepared claim fields (clause end decisions, savings, later events) are held in the producer's scratch generator and were assembled in applied-v2 and applied-v3, which rejected them for the source-record reason in the gap.

research_rationale: EO 9301 (February 9, 1943, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 8 FR 1825, issue of Thursday, February 11, 1943), read in full in the held Federal Register text, declares that "For the duration of the war" no plant or place of employment is deemed to make the most effective use of manpower if its minimum workweek is under 48 hours (section 1, inside the lead row of the machine inventory), directs agencies to require contractors to comply (2), authorizes the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission to interpret the order and issue policies, directives and regulations and to set a different workweek in particular cases (3), requires agencies to comply (4) and states that the order is not to supersede other hours or wage laws (5). EO 9607 (August 30, 1945), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in one sentence. The phrase "For the duration of the war" is an own-terms condition; no held instrument or source fixes a legal end of the war before August 30, 1945, and EO 9607 revokes the order outright without reciting that it had lapsed, so the first end is the express revocation.
savings_reason: EO 9607 consists of the revocation sentence and no saving, exception or transition wording. Obligations that contractors incurred under contracts made while EO 9301 and the War Manpower Commission's regulations were in force arise from those contracts and the regulations, not from a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any continuing effect; that is a disclosed qualification, not a finding.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is held. Own terms: section 1 begins "For the duration of the war", which ends on a legal event that no held source places before August 30, 1945 (the formal proclamation of the war's end is not held), so it is a disclosed candidate that cannot be dated and not an end. A later general rule is not shown to have ended any command. Searches of the held corpus for "Executive Order 9301" and for the minimum-workweek wording found EO 9607 (the revocation) and EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration), which cites EO 9301 in a list of orders and does not revoke or amend it. The contents table of the held Federal Register issue of August 21, 1945 (10 FR page 10166) lists a rescission of the War Manpower Commission's regulations on the minimum wartime workweek; that page is not held, so the rescission's date and text cannot be read. It would concern regulations issued under section 3, not the order, and it does not name EO 9301's revocation, so it is a disclosed earlier candidate and not an end.
scope_check: The inventory is five rows: the lead (authority recital and section 1) and sections 2 to 5. All rows end together on the revocation of the whole order; no row was amended or ended separately before then.
independent_command_check: Section 3 gives the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission authority to issue regulations and set a different workweek; it is a delegation inside the order and ends with it. Section 5 is a rule of construction protecting other laws and agreements and has no force once the order is revoked. No other independent command is found.

research_rationale: EO 9815 (December 23, 1946) replaces the proviso of section 7 of EO 9691: employment under that section may continue after the general revision of Schedule A is promulgated only if the position is included in Schedule A (the old proviso said December 31, 1946). Its text lives only as long as section 7 of EO 9691. EO 9830 lists EO 9691 in its Part III (effective May 1, 1947) and restates Schedule A, which is the event the amended proviso names, but EO 9815 itself is not on that list.

research_rationale: EO 10223 (March 10, 1951, Harry S. Truman; 16 FR 2247), read in full in the held Federal Register text, designates the Atomic Energy Commission as an additional guaranteeing agency under section 301 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 and makes sections 301, 302 and 902 of EO 10161 and EO 10182 applicable to it to the same extent as to other guaranteeing agencies; its closing sentence says nothing in the order supersedes any provision of EO 10193. It is one operative paragraph. EO 10281 (August 28, 1951), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in section 404, which is in Part IV (miscellaneous amendments); section 503 delays only Part II and section 501, so section 404 took effect on signing. The same section 404 amends section 301 of EO 10161 to insert the Atomic Energy Commission among the guaranteeing agencies. EO 10480 (August 14, 1953) lists EO 10223 again in section 607 after it was already revoked; that listing is not the first end. Prepared claim fields (clause end decisions, savings, later events) are held in the producer's scratch generator and were assembled in applied-v2 and applied-v3, which rejected them for the source-record reason in the gap.

A first end cannot cite the actor-text record (applied-v3 rejects it with clause_N_first_end and whole_order_end_evidence), and citing the transcription is rejected with working_text:official_copy_available_recheck_required because an official copy of that instrument is held (applied-v2). End found: EO 10281 section 404 (August 28, 1951) revokes EO 10223 by number; effective on signing."]

research_rationale: EO 10169 (October 11, 1950, Harry S. Truman), read in full in the held Federal Register text and the held Federal Register text, establishes the National Advisory Committee on Mobilization Policy to advise the National Security Resources Board (section 1), has the Board's Chairman appoint its members from business, labor, agriculture and the public (section 2), requests agencies to cooperate (section 3) and makes the Board defray expenses (section 4). The order has no stated term. EO 10480 (August 14, 1953), held Federal Register text, lists it in section 607 among orders "superseded or revoked". That is the first end for every section. Prepared claim fields (clause end decisions, savings, later events) are held in the producer's scratch generator and were assembled in applied-v2 and applied-v3, which rejected them for the source-record reason in the gap.

research_rationale: EO 10193 (December 16, 1950; 15 FR 9031) establishes the Office of Defense Mobilization and the Director of Defense Mobilization with seven numbered sections. EO 10461 (June 17, 1953, held) abolishes the Office and the Director's office in section 5, and EO 10480 (August 14, 1953) lists EO 10193 among orders superseded or revoked.

research_rationale: EO 10200 (January 3, 1951; 16 FR 61) assigns Defense Production Act functions (sections 1 to 6 with eighteen inventory rows, section 1(c)(5) alone about 9,500 characters). Section 1 was revoked by EO 10433 section 1(c) (February 4, 1953), EO 10281 section 405 (August 28, 1951) construes its term Defense Production Act, and EO 10480 (August 14, 1953) lists it in section 607.

research_rationale: EO 10483 (September 2, 1953) establishes the Operations Coordinating Board within the National Security Council (sections 1 to 6). EO 10598 (February 28, 1955) amends section 1; EO 10700 (February 25, 1957, held) section 6 supersedes EO 10483 and amendatory provisions, with section 7 setting the effective date at July 1, 1957.
unresolved_material_gaps: ["EO 10700 section 7 makes its provisions effective July 1, 1957 'except that if funds appropriated for the National Security Council shall not have become available on that date for the support of the Board', in which case on 'such later date as funds' become available. Whether funds were available on July 1, 1957 is not stated in any held source (an NSC appropriation record or EO 10700 implementation notice is missing), so the exact first-end date cannot be confirmed.", "EO 10610 section 303(b) proviso and EO 10598 section 1 are amendments to be recorded as later events with before-and-after text; EO 10920 (February 1961, held APP) revokes EO 10700, not EO 10483, and is not an end of this order."]

research_rationale: EO 10685 (October 27, 1956, Dwight D. Eisenhower), read in full in the held Federal Register text, has two sections. Section 1 designates the International Cooperation Administration as the Federal agency to which the Commodity Credit Corporation may transfer funds for ocean freight costs under Title II of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954. Section 2 rewrites sections 5 and 6 of EO 10560: section 5 reserves to the President the report-to-Congress function under section 108 and the designation function in the last sentence of section 203 of the Act, and section 6 defines the term Act. EO 10827 (June 25, 1959), held Federal Register text, revokes section 1 by number; that is the first end of section 1. EO 10900 (January 5, 1961; filed January 6, 1961), held Federal Register text, section 7(a)(2), supersedes EO 10685 as a whole to the extent not already superseded; that is the first end of section 2, which EO 10827 and EO 10884 changed only by replacing the section 5 text it had printed. Prepared claim fields (clause end decisions, savings, later events) are held in the producer's scratch generator and were assembled in applied-v2 and applied-v3, which rejected them for the source-record reason in the gap.
